rationale: Dallas is healthier, plays at home, and just demolished Philadelphia; Arizona at 2-5 has been inconsistent and their one win was a narrow road victory, making Dallas the safer pick here.
Atlanta is the better team by record and just beat San Francisco; Tampa Bay's 2-5 record and inconsistent play at home makes Atlanta the pick in this division matchup despite the road setting.
Buffalo is 5-1 at home and playing dominant football; Baltimore has dropped two straight including a blowout loss to Cincinnati, and the Bills' home environment gives them a clear edge.

Green Bay has won three of their last four and holds home-field advantage; Carolina's offensive line is banged up with multiple guards out, which should hamper their attack against a Packers defense playing at home.
Seattle just upset Kansas City at home and has a strong home-field advantage; Chicago lost badly to Green Bay recently and the Seahawks' home environment and momentum make them the pick here.
Pittsburgh is playing at home and has won three straight after dropping the first meeting to Cleveland; the Steelers' home-field advantage in this rivalry game makes them a slight edge pick.
Jacksonville is 4-2 with a strong home record and has won three straight before a close loss; Indianapolis at 2-5 has lost four of their last five and struggles on the road in division play.

Despite Kansas City's surprising loss to Seattle, they remain 5-1 and Patrick Mahomes historically performs well in division games; Denver is solid but KC's overall quality edges them out even on the road.
The Chargers are 0-6 and have been outclassed in every game this season; the Rams play at home in the same stadium and are a significantly better team at this point in the season.
Both teams are struggling badly, but Las Vegas has been competitive in losses while the Jets have been inconsistent at home; a slight lean to Las Vegas as the less dysfunctional squad.

Minnesota is the last undefeated team at 6-0 and has been winning close games consistently; Detroit is dangerous at home but the Vikings' unbeaten run and overall team quality gives them the edge in this division showdown.
New England has won three straight and is playing quality football; Miami at 1-5 has been one of the worst teams in the AFC and even home-field advantage cannot overcome that gap.
Both teams are struggling, but Philadelphia has more talent and Washington is 1-4 at home; the Eagles' roster depth gives them a slight edge despite their own poor recent form.
Cincinnati is 4-2, playing at home, and just demolished Baltimore; Tennessee at 1-6 is one of the worst teams in the league and this should be a comfortable Bengals win.
